greek_asclepius.name: Cure the sick through dream-vision in temple incubation
greek_asclepius.notes: At the Asclepieia the sick slept in the abaton and the god appeared in a dream to prescribe or directly effect the cure; the iamata stelai of Epidaurus record the miracle-cures.

greek_asclepius.name: Stay disease and wounds as the gentlest of physicians
greek_asclepius.notes: Trained by Chiron, he surpassed all in surgery, drugs and the soothing of pain; Pindar lists his cures of ulcers, fevers and wounds.

greek_asclepius.name: Raise the dead with the Gorgon's blood
greek_asclepius.notes: Using blood drawn from Medusa's left side (given him by Athena) he restored the dead to life until Zeus, to preserve the boundary of mortality, killed him with a thunderbolt.

greek_eileithyia.name: Loose or bind the womb to release or arrest childbirth
greek_eileithyia.notes: As 'she who loosens the girdle' she brings on delivery; by crossing her legs and fingers outside Alcmene's chamber she held back the birth of Heracles for seven days.

greek_eileithyia.name: Bring the child out of darkness into the light
greek_eileithyia.notes: The Eileithyiai are the daughters of Hera who hold the keen pangs of travail and bring children forth; without her present no birth can be completed.

greek_deimos.name: Drive the ranks of men into dread and rout beside Ares
greek_deimos.notes: With his brother Phobos he yokes the chariot of Ares and looses terror through the battle-lines (Theogony 934; Iliad 4.440, 15.119).

greek_cassandra.name: Foresee the future truly yet never be believed
greek_cassandra.notes: Apollo's double gift: she prophesied the fall of Troy, the doom of the wooden horse and her own and Agamemnon's deaths, all in vain.

greek_castor.name: Save sailors from storm as a saviour of ships
greek_castor.notes: With Pollux the Dioscuri appear in tempest as the twin lights (St Elmo's fire) on the masthead and calm the sea for mariners.

greek_apollod_telephus.name: Be wounded and healed by the same Achillean spear
greek_apollod_telephus.notes: Speared by Achilles at the Mysian landing, his unhealing wound could be cured only by the rust of the spear that made it ('the wounder heals'), the price of guiding the Greeks to Troy.

greek_atreus.name: Claim the throne of Mycenae by the portent of the golden lamb
greek_atreus.notes: The golden lamb in his flock marked the rightful king; though Aerope stole it for Thyestes, Zeus reversed the sun's course to vindicate Atreus's title.

greek_atreus.name: Take vengeance by the Thyestean feast
greek_atreus.notes: He slew Thyestes' sons and served them to their father at a banquet, the founding crime of the curse on the house of Atreus.

greek_clytemnestra.name: Snare and slay the returning king
greek_clytemnestra.notes: She cast an inescapable robe-net over Agamemnon in the bath and struck him down with an axe, avenging Iphigenia.

greek_cycnus_poseidon.name: Be transformed by Poseidon into a swan at death
greek_cycnus_poseidon.notes: When Achilles strangled the invulnerable king with his own helmet-strap, Poseidon changed his vanishing body into the swan (kyknos) for which he was named.

greek_ceyx.name: Be transformed with Alcyone into the halcyon birds
greek_ceyx.notes: Drowned in a storm and mourned by his faithful wife, the gods in pity turned the pair into kingfishers; the windless 'halcyon days' mark her brooding on the calmed winter sea.

greek_epaphus.name: Found Memphis and rule Egypt as the touch-born son of Zeus
greek_epaphus.notes: Born by the touch (epaphe) of Zeus on the restored Io at the Nile; he founded Memphis and from him descend the Libyans, Aethiopians and (through Libya) the Argive, Phoenician and Theban lines.

greek_callisto.name: Be transformed into a bear and set among the stars
greek_callisto.notes: Turned into a bear (by Hera, Artemis, or Zeus in the variants) for the union with Zeus; saved from her son's spear, she was catasterised as Ursa Major, the Great Bear.

greek_chione_boread.name: Bear Eumolpus to Poseidon and be saved by the sea
greek_chione_boread.notes: The snow-nymph daughter of Boreas bore Eumolpus to Poseidon and, to hide her shame, cast him into the sea, where his father received and reared him.

greek_chrysippus.name: Occasion the curse of the Theban house by his abduction
greek_chrysippus.notes: Carried off (and violated) by the exiled Laius, whom Pelops was teaching to drive a chariot; Pelops' curse on Laius for the rape sets in motion the doom of Oedipus and Thebes.

greek_deiphobus.name: Fight as the bravest Trojan prince after Hector
greek_deiphobus.notes: Athena took his likeness to lure Hector to his death; he wed Helen after Paris fell and was killed and mutilated by Menelaus at the sack.

greek_astyanax.name: Embody the extinguished heir of Troy
greek_astyanax.notes: The infant 'lord of the city' (Scamandrius to his father), thrown from the walls at the sack so no scion of Priam's house should survive to avenge it.

greek_aristaeus.name: The beehive and the ox-born bees (bugonia)
greek_aristaeus.notes: Inventor of apiculture; in the Georgics his lost bees are regenerated from the carcass of a sacrificed ox (bugonia), the ritual remedy taught by Proteus and Cyrene.

greek_asclepius.name: The chryselephantine cult-statue enthroned with staff and dog at Epidaurus

sources.reference: Pausanias, Description of Greece 2.27.2 (statue by Thrasymedes)

greek_eileithyia.name: Twin torches of childbirth (light brought to the newborn)

sources.reference: Theoi Project s.v. Eileithyia, citing votive reliefs

greek_apollod_telephus.name: The rust-cure of the Achillean spear (telephus' remedy)

greek_castor.name: The pilos cap crowned with a star

greek_bellerophon.name: The lead-tipped spear that slew the Chimera
greek_bellerophon.notes: In Apollodorus he fixed a lump of lead to his spear-point; the Chimera's fiery breath melted it and the molten metal killed the monster.

greek_clymene_merops.name: The chariot of Helios (sought by her son Phaethon)
greek_clymene_merops.notes: Clymene's revelation of Phaethon's solar paternity sends him to claim the chariot of the Sun, the proof of his birth.

sources.reference: Pergamon, Telephus frieze of the Great Altar

greek_eileithyia.gloss: She who brings to light (Roman name)

sources.reference: Homer, Odyssey 19.188; Linear B Am-ni-so e-re-u-ti-ja

greek_cassandra.gloss: Defender of men (her cult-name in Laconia)

greek_castor.gloss: the Lords (joint title of the Dioscuri)

sources.reference: Etymological wordplay in Apollodorus 2.7.4 (suckled by a deer)

greek_dardanus.gloss: eponym of the Dardanians and Dardania

greek_asclepius.name: Incubation healing at the Asclepieia
greek_asclepius.notes: Pilgrims purified, sacrificed (often a cock), and slept in the abaton to be cured by the god in a dream; Epidaurus was the mother-sanctuary of some two hundred Asclepieia. Votive body-part models and the iamata stelai attest the cures.

sources.reference: Pausanias, Description of Greece 2.27; Epidaurus iamata

greek_asclepius.name: The Epidauria at Athens
greek_asclepius.notes: Festival within the Eleusinian Mysteries commemorating the god's arrival in Athens (420 BCE) when Sophocles received the sacred snake; the cult travelled from Epidaurus to the south slope of the Acropolis.

sources.reference: Plutarch, Life of Numa; IG II2 4960 (Telemachos monument)

greek_eileithyia.name: Cave-cult of Eileithyia at Amnisos
greek_eileithyia.notes: Her oldest sanctuary, the cave near Amnisos in Crete, received offerings from Minoan times into the Roman period; she is named already on Linear B tablets. Shrines also at Athens, Tegea, Argos and Aigion.

greek_apollod_theseus.name: The Theseia
greek_apollod_theseus.notes: Instituted after Cimon brought the hero's bones from Skyros (c. 475 BCE) and built the Theseion; celebrated on the eighth of Pyanepsion with procession, sacrifice, a torch-race and athletic and martial contests.

sources.reference: Plutarch, Life of Theseus 35-36; Life of Cimon 8

greek_deimos.name: Joint cult of Phobos and Deimos at Sparta
greek_deimos.notes: The Spartans honoured Fear and Dread as guarantors of military discipline; warriors swore oaths and sacrificed to them before battle (the bull slaughtered over the black shield in Seven Against Thebes).

sources.reference: Plutarch, Life of Cleomenes 9; Aeschylus, Seven Against Thebes 42-48

greek_castor.name: The Anakeia (cult of the Dioscuri)
greek_castor.notes: At Sparta the twins were venerated at Therapne with the aniconic dokana (twin beams) carried into battle beside the kings; at Athens at the Anakeion. They received both burnt sacrifice as gods and libations as the dead.

greek_cassandra.name: Cult of Alexandra-Cassandra in Laconia
greek_cassandra.notes: Worshipped as a heroine under the name Alexandra: a sanctuary and statue with that of Agamemnon at Amyclae, and a temple with cult-statue at Leuctra in Laconia.

greek_aristaeus.name: Cult of Aristaeus on Ceos
greek_aristaeus.notes: On Ceos he was credited with ending a deadly drought by raising an altar to Zeus Ikmaios and summoning the cooling Etesian winds; honoured as patron of beekeeping, herding and olive-culture in Boeotia, Thessaly, Ceos, Sardinia and Cyrene.

greek_apollod_telephus.name: Hero-cult of Telephus at Pergamon
greek_apollod_telephus.notes: Founder-hero and dynastic ancestor of the Attalids, whose genealogy the Telephus frieze of the Great Altar traced from his birth to his healing; he was suckled by a she-lion.

sources.reference: Pergamon, Telephus frieze of the Great Altar (Berlin)

greek_cyrene_lapith.name: Cult of Cyrene at the Libyan colony
greek_cyrene_lapith.notes: Eponymous nymph and tutelary heroine of the polis of Cyrene, where the Delphic oracle directed the founder Battus; her abduction by Apollo founds the city in Pindar's ode.

greek_arcas.name: Hero-cult and tomb of Arcas at Mantineia
greek_arcas.notes: On the Delphic oracle's command his bones were translated from Mount Maenalus and re-buried beside the altar of Hera at Mantineia, where his grave was shown.

attributes.name: Youthful herdsman, sometimes winged, among his hives and flocks
attributes.notes: In Boeotian vase-painting he may appear as a winged youth like the Boreads; otherwise a young shepherd-figure associated with bees, the olive and the milking-pail.

sacredAnimals.name: Bee (his emblem as the god who gave men beekeeping)

sacredPlants.name: Olive and silphium (the cultivated plants in his gift)

attributes.name: Bearded mature man in a himation leaning on the serpent-staff
attributes.notes: The canonical type: a benign full-bearded figure, chest bare, resting on a knotty staff entwined by a single serpent, sometimes with a dog at his feet.

sacredAnimals.name: Serpent (the Aesculapian rat-snake that licked wounds in the abaton)
Dog (the sacred dogs of Epidaurus that healed by licking)

attributes.name: Veiled woman with a raised torch or with both arms lifted
attributes.notes: Shown bringing the child 'to the light': either holding torches (with Artemis and Persephone) or with arms thrown up in the gesture of delivery.

sources.reference: Theoi Project s.v. Eileithyia, citing votive reliefs

attributes.name: Beardless youthful athlete with club or sword over the fallen Minotaur
attributes.notes: In Attic vase-painting the type-scene shows the young hero dragging or striking the bull-headed Minotaur; he wears a short chiton and carries a sword or the club won from Periphetes.

sources.reference: Attic black- and red-figure Minotauromachy vases; Pausanias 1.17.2-3

sacredAnimals.name: Bull (the Marathonian/Cretan bull and the Minotaur he mastered)

attributes.name: Fearsome face blazoned on the warrior's shield
attributes.notes: With Phobos, Deimos was engraved around the Gorgon-head on the shields of heroes (Agamemnon's in Iliad 11; the Shield of Heracles).

attributes.name: Egg-shaped pilos cap surmounted by a star
attributes.notes: The Dioscuri wear the conical felt cap (from the egg of their birth) crowned with a star, and carry spears.

sacredAnimals.name: Horse (Castor's mount Cyllarus; the twins as the great horsemen)
Lioness (the she-lion that suckled the exposed infant)

sources.reference: Pergamon, Telephus frieze of the Great Altar

sacredAnimals.name: Hind/deer (the doe that nursed him, source of his name)

attributes.name: Huntress wrestling or strangling a lion
attributes.notes: Pindar's 'lion-slaying' maiden; the motif of Cyrene throttling the lion (with Libya crowning her) appears in Cyrenean coinage and reliefs.

sacredAnimals.name: Bear (her transformed shape and the constellation Ursa Major)
Crow/raven (whose feathers Apollo scorched black; the constellation Corvus)
Halcyon / kingfisher (the bird he and Alcyone became)
Bull (identified by the Greeks with the Egyptian Apis bull)
Pegasus (the winged horse he tamed and rode)

attributes.name: Winged youth with dusky, gold-scaled wings at shoulders and ankles
attributes.notes: The Boread twins are shown as winged runners; over their tombs on Tenos the pillars were said to sway when the north wind blew.
